selection.objective: Mean squared error of original two-class logit margin, equal weight to ordinary/high-density groups and equal weight to sequences within each group.
selection.accuracy: Lowest calibration margin MSE; equivalent synaptic AC breaks ties.
selection.low_spike: Lowest equivalent synaptic AC among searched candidates whose margin MSE is no worse than uncalibrated at the same T in BOTH density groups; otherwise retain uncalibrated. This is selection, never an execution guard.
selection.search: Stagewise coordinate grid search, two coarse passes followed by two local integer-threshold/membrane refinement passes; archive all evaluated candidates. The refinement was added after the Train-main coarse search retained the default, BEFORE any Dev evaluation. No gradient, optimizer, weight update or Train-dev feedback. r2 starts from the r1 accuracy calibration and also includes the original default.

encoding.parameters: One positive integer threshold theta and initial membrane m0 in [0,theta) per converted hidden layer, shared across channels.
encoding.update: v += original uint8 activation a; fire at most one binary spike if v>=theta; subtract theta on firing.
encoding.decode: sum(original_int8_weight_per_spike) * original_output_scale / T * theta / 255; default theta=255 uses exactly the original direct_v1 arithmetic.
encoding.saturation: a>theta saturates at one spike per tick; count and disclose these cells, do not stop the run.
encoding.unchanged: Proposal, candidate gating, C1 36-dimensional features, 36-64-32-4 bias-free Refiner, all weight/scale arrays, original uint8 quantizers, prototype readout, 0.35 decision threshold, closed 100ms windows.

evaluation: Freeze selections on deterministic Train-main subset, then evaluate uncalibrated/accuracy/low_spike on all ten Train-dev sequences. Every calibrated point uses explicit binary spike additions and checks full logits against the analytic count reference.
limitations: Layer-serial hybrid network, not fully spiking or pipelined. T is coding steps, not milliseconds. Neural MAC/AC exclude some feature/routing/readout/memory costs; no hardware energy or latency claim.
